name: Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Bangui
subtitle: Historic red-brick cathedral where Pope Francis inaugurated the Holy Door of the 2015 Jubilee of Mercy.

facts.label: Construction
facts.value: Built in the 1930s with local red brick

facts.label: Ecumenical milestone
facts.value: Pope Francis opened the Jubilee Holy Door on 29 November 2015

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Spiritual anchor and sanctuary during periods of civil conflict

parts.text: The primary Catholic cathedral of the Central African Republic, situated in central Bangui near the banks of the Ubangi River. Constructed in the 1930s out of striking kiln-fired red bricks in a neo-Romanesque design, it gained worldwide renown on 29 November 2015 when Pope Francis made an unprecedented apostolic journey amidst civil strife, personally opening its Holy Door to inaugurate the Extraordinary Jubilee of Mercy—the first time in modern papal history that a Holy Year was opened outside of Rome—proclaiming Bangui as the spiritual capital of peace for the world.

gaps: Diocesan architectural blueprints and stained-glass restoration records remain uncatalogued online.
